# The Showers That Surprise

## Scripture

*"Be patient, then, brothers and sisters, until the Lord's coming. See how the farmer waits for the land to yield its valuable crop, patiently waiting for the autumn and spring rains."* — James 5:7 (NIV)

## Reflection

November brings the Leonids—a meteor shower that sparks across the sky when Earth passes through debris left by Comet Tempel-Tuttle. Most years the display is modest. But occasionally, unpredictably, the heavens erupt in a shower of light. No one can say exactly when.

James understood that kind of waiting. He pointed farmers toward the autumn rains—not because rain never comes, but because it comes in its season, and the waiting itself is part of the harvest. The farmer cannot hurry the sky. He can only prepare the soil, tend the field, and trust.

Perhaps you are in a season of waiting right now. A prayer unanswered. A promise that feels delayed. The sky above you may look ordinary, star by star, with no sign of breakthrough. But the God who orchestrates comet debris and raindrops keeps a calendar you cannot read. His timing is not delay—it is cultivation.

The Leonids remind us that surprises are written into creation. The universe is not static; it is full of appointed moments. So is your life. What feels like empty sky may simply be the quiet before the shower.

Wait with hope. The One who set the comet on its path has not forgotten yours.

## Prayer

Lord of the seasons, teach us to wait with patient, hopeful hearts. When the sky seems quiet, remind us that You are preparing something we cannot yet see. Strengthen our faith in Your perfect timing, and let us trust the harvest You are growing in us. Amen.
